# TW Framework — Complete Reference for AI Coding Assistants
# Source: https://github.com/ffakraj-ui/twlang
# Version: v0.8.45 (2026-08-10)
# Rule: If README and source code disagree, trust the source code and tests.

---

## 1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

TW Framework (package: `tw-framework` on PyPI) is a Python-based full-stack web framework with App Router, Zero-JS static sites, NPM package manager, React compatibility, and esbuild bundling.

- **Language**: Custom DSL (`.tw` pages/components/layouts, `.tss` stylesheets, `.twm` API routes)
- **Runtime**: Python (compiler + dev server + CLI). API routes (`.twm`) run on Node.js.
- **Package manager**: `pip install tw-framework` (Python). NPM packages via `tw install` command.
- **File extensions**: `.tw` (pages/components/layouts), `.tss` (stylesheets), `.twm` (API routes/lib modules), `.js`/`.ts` (client libraries)
- **Project root marker**: `tw.config` file
- **Source folder**: `[home]/` (literal brackets — App Router root)

### 1.1 Installation
```bash
pip install tw-framework
```

### 1.2 Quick Start
```bash
pip install tw-framework
tw create my-site
cd my-site
tw dev
```

### 1.3 Build
```bash
tw build       # outputs to dist/
tw serve       # production SSR server
```

---

## 2. PROJECT STRUCTURE

```
my-site/
  tw.config              # project config
  .env                   # environment variables
  middleware.tw          # middleware (auth, headers, rewrites)
  [home]/                 # App Router root (literal brackets)
    layout.tw            # root layout (wraps all pages)
    page.tw              # home page (/)
    not-found.tw         # 404 page
    style.tss            # global stylesheet
    about/page.tw        # /about
    blog/page.tw         # /blog (index)
    blog/[slug]/page.tw  # /blog/:slug (dynamic route)
    blog/posts.json      # data for dynamic routes
    counter/page.tw      # /counter
    contact/page.tw      # /contact
    components/           # reusable components
      Navbar.tw
      Footer.tw
      Button.tw
      Card.tw
    lib/                  # JavaScript libraries
      countdown.js
    api/                  # API routes (server-only)
      contact/route.tw
      users/route.tw
    assets/               # images, fonts, etc.
  public/                 # static files (copied as-is to dist/)
    robots.txt
    sitemap.xml
    favicon.ico
  dist/                   # build output
```

### 2.1 Public Folder
Files in `public/` are served as-is (no compilation). Allowed: `.txt`, `.html`, `.css`, `.js`, `.xml`, `.ico`, images, fonts. NOT allowed: `.tw`, `.tss`, `.twm` (use `[home]/` for those).

---

## 3. TW SYNTAX (.tw FILES)

TW uses block-based syntax with curly braces. NOT JSX, NOT HTML angle brackets.

### 3.1 Page Block
```tw
page {
    title "My Page"
    render static
}
```

### 3.2 Render Modes
```tw
render static       # SSG — build-time HTML (default)
render server       # SSR — server-side render per request
render edge         # Edge runtime
render interactive  # client-side hydration (React)
render dynamic      # auto-detect: state/for/if → server, else static
```

### 3.3 Page Directives
```tw
page {
    title "Blog Post"
    render static
    generateStaticParams "posts.json"   # dynamic route pre-rendering
    revalidate 60                        # ISR — re-generate every 60s
    redirect "/new-path"                 # redirect this page
    rewrite "/other-page"                # rewrite to another route
    cache_by "cookie:lang"              # cache key
    cache_size 100                      # cache limit
}
```

### 3.4 Body
```tw
body {
    h1 "Hello World"
    p "This is a paragraph."
    div { class "card"
        h2 "Title"
        p "Content"
    }
    a "Click me" { href "/about", class "link" }
}
```

### 3.5 Text Interpolation
```tw
h1 "Hello {name}"
p "Count: {count}"
a { href "/blog/{post.slug}" text "Read more" }
```

### 3.6 Attributes
```tw
div { class "container", id "main", data-value "123"
    p "Content"
}
img { src "/photo.jpg", alt "Photo", width 800, height 600 }
input { type "text", name "email", placeholder "Email", required true }
```

---

## 4. IMPORTS

TW supports TWO import syntaxes:

### 4.1 Component Import (old syntax)
```tw
import "Navbar"
import "Button"
```
Loads a `.tw` component from `[home]/components/`. Use the component as a tag:
```tw
body {
    Navbar {}
    Button { href "/about", label "Click" }
}
```

### 4.2 ES6 Library Import (v0.8.45+)
```tw
import { startCountdown } from "@/lib/countdown"
import { formatData, parseJSON } from "@/lib/utils"
```
Loads a `.js`/`.ts`/`.mjs` file from `[home]/lib/`. Use functions in script blocks:
```tw
body {
    div { id "countdown" }
    script { startCountdown() }
}
```

### 4.3 Load Directive (data/styles/modules)
```tw
load "@/blog/posts.json"        # JSON data (key auto-inferred from filename)
load "@/style.tss"               # stylesheet
load "@/lib/auth"                # .twm module (server-side)
```

### 4.4 Script Blocks
Inline scripts: `script { console.log("hello") }` — raw JS, written as-is.
**{prop} interpolation now works in scripts** (v0.8.45+):
```tw
let target "2025-12-31"
body {
    script { new Date("{target}").getFullYear() }
}
```
External scripts: `script { src "@/lib/helper.js" }` — @/ is resolved and
file is copied to `dist/_tw/scripts/` (v0.8.45+). Also supports absolute URLs:
`script { src "https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" }`.

---

## 5. COMPONENTS

### 5.1 Creating Components
File: `[home]/components/Button.tw`
```tw
a { class "btn", href "{href}"
    text "{label}"
}
```

### 5.2 Using Components (Auto-Discovery)
Components in `[home]/components/` are **auto-discovered**. No `import` needed:
```tw
body {
    Navbar {}
    Button { href "/about", label "Get Started" }
}
```
`import "Button"` also works but is optional.

### 5.3 Scoped CSS (v0.8.37+)
File: `[home]/components/Button.tss`
```tss
btn-primary {
    background blue
    color white
    padding 12 24
}
```
CSS is automatically scoped to the component via `data-tw-{hash}` attribute. `@media` queries preserved, `@keyframes` stay global.

---

## 6. LAYOUTS

### 6.1 Root Layout
File: `[home]/layout.tw`
```tw
page {
    title "My Site"
    render static
}

load "@/style.tss"

head {
    meta { charset "utf-8" }
    meta { name "viewport", content "width=device-width, initial-scale=1" }
    seo {
        description "Site description"
    }
}

body {
    Navbar {}
    main { class "main-content"
        children
    }
    Footer {}
}
```

The `children` keyword injects page content into the layout.

---

## 7. DYNAMIC ROUTES

### 7.1 File Structure
```
[home]/blog/[slug]/page.tw    # dynamic route: /blog/:slug
[home]/blog/posts.json        # data file
```

### 7.2 Page with generateStaticParams
```tw
page {
    title "{title}"
    render static
    generateStaticParams "posts.json"
}

body {
    article { class "blog-post"
        h1 "{title}"
        p "{excerpt}"
    }
}
```

### 7.3 JSON Data File
```json
[
    {"slug": "post-1", "title": "First Post", "excerpt": "Content..."},
    {"slug": "post-2", "title": "Second Post", "excerpt": "Content..."}
]
```

Each item in the JSON array generates a static page. The slug field becomes the URL.

### 7.4 Blog Index Page
```tw
page {
    title "Blog"
    render static
}

load "@/blog/posts.json"

body {
    each posts as post {
        a { class "blog-card", href "/blog/{post.slug}"
            h2 "{post.title}"
            p "{post.excerpt}"
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 8. STATE MANAGEMENT (Reactivity)

```tw
page {
    title "Counter"
    render static
}

state {
    count 0
    name "Guest"
}

body {
    h1 "Count: {count}"
    button {
        on:click "__tw.set('count', __tw.get('count') + 1)"
        class "btn"
        text "+"
    }
    button {
        on:click "__tw.set('count', 0)"
        class "btn"
        text "Reset"
    }
}
```

State uses `__tw.set(key, value)` and `__tw.get(key)`. Changes auto-re-render the page.

---

## 9. CONDITIONAL RENDERING

```tw
body {
    if isLoggedIn {
        h1 "Welcome back!"
    }
    else {
        h1 "Please log in"
    }
}
```

---

## 10. LOOPS

```tw
load "@/blog/posts.json"

body {
    each posts as post {
        div { class "card"
            h2 "{post.title}"
            p "{post.excerpt}"
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 11. TSS STYLESHEETS (.tss FILES)

```tss
body {
    margin 0
    font-family system-ui, sans-serif
    background var(--bg)
    color var(--fg)
}

:root {
    --bg #ffffff
    --fg #0b1220
}

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
    --bg #0f172a
    --fg #e2e8f0
}

.btn {
    display inline-block
    padding 14 32
    border-radius 12
    background var(--accent)
    color white
}

@media (max-width: 768) {
    .btn { width 100% }
}

@keyframes fadeIn {
    from { opacity 0 }
    to { opacity 1 }
}
```

TSS uses space-separated values (not colons/semicolons). Numbers without units get `px`.

---

## 12. API ROUTES (.twm FILES)

File: `[home]/api/contact/route.tw`
```tw
fn post(request) {
    return {
        status: 200,
        json: { ok: true, message: "Thanks!", received: request.body || {} }
    };
}

fn get(request) {
    return {
        status: 200,
        json: [{ id: 1, name: "Ada" }, { id: 2, name: "Grace" }]
    };
}
```

Methods: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options`. API routes are server-only, not included in `dist/`.

---

## 13. MIDDLEWARE

File: `middleware.tw`
```tw
use {
    match "/dashboard/**"
    auth "session" "/"
    header "X-Frame-Options" "DENY"
}
```

---

## 14. tw.config OPTIONS

```
name: My TW Site
site_url: https://example.com
description: Site description
theme: system
pretty_urls: true
search: true
modular_pipeline: true
allow_raw_script: true
sitemap: true
robots: true
rss: true
auto_image_alt: true
```

### 14.1 Sitemap/Robots/RSS (v0.8.42+ — Opt-in)
All three default to OFF. Set to `true` to enable auto-generation.

Priority: developer file > auto-generated. If you place `public/sitemap.xml`, `public/robots.txt`, or `public/rss.xml`, TW uses your file instead of generating its own.

### 14.2 XSL Sitemap Styling (v0.8.42+)
When sitemap is auto-generated, TW also creates `sitemap.xsl` — a stylesheet that makes `/sitemap.xml` render as a styled page in the browser. Place your own `public/sitemap.xsl` to customize.

### 14.3 Auto Image Alt (v0.8.42+)
When `auto_image_alt: true`, images without an `alt` attribute get auto-generated alt from filename (first 8 chars, hyphens/underscores → spaces). Example: `/img/my-profile-photo.jpg` → `alt="my profi"`.

---

## 15. IMAGE OPTIMIZATION (v0.8.37+)

Two image tags:
- `image { src "..." alt "..." width 800 height 600 }` → optimized (lazy loading, srcset, responsive, decoding async)
- `img { src "..." alt "..." }` → normal (no optimization)

Developer chooses which to use.

---

## 16. CLI COMMANDS

```bash
tw create <name>           # create new project
tw dev                     # start dev server (http://127.0.0.1:3000)
tw build                   # build to dist/
tw serve                   # production server (SSR + API)
tw serve --port 8000       # custom port
tw preview                 # preview built site
tw install <pkg>           # install npm package (react, lodash, etc.)
tw clean                   # clear cache and dist
tw doctor                  # check project health
tw info                    # show project info
tw export                  # export static site
tw deploy                  # deploy (adapter-based)
tw analyze                 # analyze build output
```

---

## 17. NPM PACKAGES

```bash
tw install react react-dom    # install npm packages
tw install lodash              # install any npm package
```

Packages go to `node_modules/`. TW auto-bundles imports from node_modules using esbuild. React is auto-detected and bundled from node_modules when installed.

---

## 18. BUILD FEATURES

### 18.1 Zero JS by Default
Static pages produce pure HTML + CSS. No JavaScript unless:
- `render interactive` (React hydration)
- `state {}` block (reactivity)
- `on:click` events
- `script {}` blocks

### 18.2 Code Splitting
TW auto-splits shared chunks (CSS, JS) across pages.

### 18.3 Incremental Build (v0.8.37+)
Modified files are tracked. Only changed pages are rebuilt. Cache hit rate shown in build stats.

### 18.4 Error Overlay (v0.8.37+)
Dev server shows a styled error overlay with source code, line numbers, and suggestions when a `.tw` file has syntax errors.

### 18.5 Dev Server Auto-Reload
Edit `.tw`, `.tss`, `.ts` files — browser auto-reloads via Server-Sent Events.

---

## 19. SEO

```tw
page {
    title "My Page"
    render static
}

head {
    seo {
        description "Page description"
        keywords "keyword1, keyword2"
        og-title "Open Graph Title"
        og-image "/img/og.jpg"
        json-ld {
            "@type": "Article",
            "headline": "My Article"
        }
    }
}
```

---

## 20. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES

File: `.env`
```
SITE_NAME=My Site
API_TOKEN=change-me
```

Use in pages:
```tw
page {
    title "{env.SITE_NAME}"
}
```

Public env vars (exposed to client) configured in tw.config:
```
env:
  public: "SITE_NAME,API_TOKEN"
```

---

## 21. COMMON PATTERNS

### 21.1 Full Page Example
```tw
import "Navbar"
import "Footer"
import { startCountdown } from "@/lib/countdown"

page {
    title "Home"
    render static
}

load "@/style.tss"

body {
    Navbar {}
    section { class "hero"
        h1 "Welcome"
        p "Build modern web apps"
        Button { href "/about", label "Learn More" }
    }
    Footer {}
}
```

### 21.2 API Route Example
```tw
fn get(request) {
    return {
        status: 200,
        json: { users: [{ id: 1, name: "Ada" }] }
    };
}

fn post(request) {
    return {
        status: 201,
        json: { ok: true, id: 999 }
    };
}
```

---

## 22. ERROR REFERENCE

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| TW1000 | Parser error (syntax) |
| TW2001 | Undefined symbol |
| TW2002 | Type mismatch |
| TW3001 | Missing required attribute |
| TW3102 | generateStaticParams JSON shape error |

---

## 23. WHAT TW IS NOT

- TW is NOT React (no JSX, no `function Page()`, no `useState`)
- TW is NOT Next.js (no `export default`, no `getStaticProps`)
- TW is NOT Vue (no `<template>`, no `v-if`)
- TW has its own syntax: `page { }`, `body { }`, `state { }`, `each ... as ... { }`
- TW CAN use React via `render interactive` + `tw install react react-dom`

---

End of reference. Always trust the source code and tests over documentation.
